title: Central Authorization Unit Guidelines for Insured Plan of Care Requests
content:
**Insured Plan of Care — authorization requests to the payer.** An authorization request is initial, extension, retroactive, peer-to-peer or appeal. The guidelines below govern when each is submitted and how an answer is recorded.

## Guidelines

1. **Status.** Authorization requests are submitted only while the plan is in intake, active or on hold status.
2. **Extension requests.** Where the payer program requires prior authorization, an extension request is submitted once the remaining authorized visits fall to the payer program's extension trigger or fewer, and in any case no later than the payer program's extension lead days, in calendar days, before the current authorization end date.
3. **Follow-up.** A request still pending after the payer program's follow-up period, in business days, is followed up with the payer.
4. **Retroactive requests.** A retroactive authorization request is submitted no later than the payer program's retroactive window, in calendar days, after the visit date of the earliest visit it asks to cover. Days are counted as calendar days from the visit date, the visit date itself being day zero. A retroactive window of 0 means the payer accepts no retroactive request, and visits rendered without authorization are then written off and never billed to the patient.
5. **Peer-to-peer and appeal.** After a denial, a peer-to-peer request may be made within the payer program's peer-to-peer window in calendar days, and a written appeal is submitted no later than the payer program's appeal window, in calendar days, after the date the denial was received. Days are counted as calendar days from the denial date, the denial date itself being day zero. A peer-to-peer request or appeal carries the reference of the denial it contests.
6. **Approvals.** An approval records its authorization number, date span and approved visits, and the plan's current authorization number and end date are updated to the newest approval.
7. **Hold for authorization.** An active plan whose authorized visits are exhausted or whose authorization has ended is placed on hold for authorization until a new approval arrives.

**Evidence.** The plan's status, the visit dates of its visits and the receipt date of a denial are read from the plan's system records; the denial an appeal contests is identified by its reference.

## Window boundaries (hypothetical dates, using scheduled windows)

| Request | Day zero | Window | Last day within the window | First day outside it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retroactive, Commercial POS Plan of Care | Earliest visit 2026-03-10 | 14 calendar days | 2026-03-24 | 2026-03-25 |
| Retroactive, Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | Earliest visit 2026-03-10 | 30 calendar days | 2026-04-09 | 2026-04-10 |
| Retroactive, a program with a window of 0 | — | none | No retroactive request is accepted | — |
| Written appeal, Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | Denial received 2026-02-01 | 60 calendar days | 2026-04-02 | 2026-04-03 |

## Extension timing (hypothetical)

On a Commercial POS plan (extension trigger 2 visits, lead 7 calendar days) whose current authorization ends on 2026-05-31, an extension request is due once 2 or fewer authorized visits remain, and in any case by 2026-05-24.
